cohortSelection: Twelve records from a present-day compiled July PDUFA calendar, not a frozen pre-July PDUFA universe. July 11 relacorilant was already FDA approved by March and excluded.
method: Independent Level-3-style desk research using cited sponsor pages published before July 2026. Clinical efficacy, patient-benefit/risk, and regulatory/CMC fit. Frozen as research calls but not truly blind because some outcome information had previously been seen; never portray this as blind validation.

predictions.level1ClinicalEvidence: Sponsor reported SPARKLE Phase 3 primary imaging visualization endpoint positive in renal impairment; Phase 2 liver lesion detection evidence supportive.
predictions.level2BenefitRisk: Diagnostic unmet need for patients in whom standard contrast use is difficult, with reported mild adverse events; agreement of independent imaging readers and lesion detection validation remain uncertain.
predictions.level3RegulatoryFit: Approval lean from positive pivotal imaging program and accepted NDA, but reader/endpoint adequacy, data package and CMC are material risks.

predictions.level1ClinicalEvidence: Randomized Phase 3 Precision-T reported 78% survival without moderate/severe chronic GvHD versus 38% transplant control at one year.
predictions.level2BenefitRisk: Strong effect on patient-important graft outcomes, though donor selection, infectious complications and OS uncertainty require review.
predictions.level3RegulatoryFit: Approval lean because large pivotal efficacy signal and BLA under review; however April major amendment for updated CMC and extended review is serious manufacturing risk.

predictions.level1ClinicalEvidence: Randomized Phase 3 IgA nephropathy trial demonstrated clinically favorable proteinuria response; long-term eGFR data for full approval planned later.
predictions.level2BenefitRisk: IgAN biologic plausibility and proteinuria surrogate support accelerated pathway; kidney-function durability and infection/immunosuppressive risk unresolved.
predictions.level3RegulatoryFit: Approval lean for accelerated proteinuria-lowering indication, not evidence of final kidney-function outcome or full approval; sponsor-reported FDA discussions and July goal supportive.

predictions.application: Enhertu DESTINY-Breast05 post-neoadjuvant HER2+ breast cancer
predictions.level1ClinicalEvidence: Randomized Phase 3 demonstrated IDFS HR 0.47 (95% CI 0.34–0.66) compared with T-DM1; priority review accepted.
predictions.level2BenefitRisk: Strong post-neoadjuvant recurrence prevention; interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis and tolerability are counterweights, OS immature.
predictions.level3RegulatoryFit: Approval lean in approved anti-HER2 drug family with statistically strong pivotal IDFS and supportive regulatory pathway.

predictions.level1ClinicalEvidence: Sponsor April 10, 2026 release explicitly reports drug already FDA-approved in March 2026.
predictions.level2BenefitRisk: As of the cutoff, FDA disposition was publicly known and no July undecided application remained.
predictions.level3RegulatoryFit: EXCLUDE: July 11 originally disclosed target is stale for a 2026-06-30-origin blind-test eligibility roster. Do not generate a July approval/CRL prediction.

predictions.application: Gedatolisib (Revtorpyk) for PIK3CA-WT advanced breast cancer
predictions.level1ClinicalEvidence: Pivotal randomized VIKTORIA-1 wild-type cohort reported significant PFS benefit for gedatolisib regimens; FDA accepted NDA priority review.
predictions.level2BenefitRisk: PFS improvement after endocrine progression supports efficacy, though combined regimen toxicity, dose interruptions and OS maturity are concerns.
predictions.level3RegulatoryFit: Approval lean with RTOR, priority review, breakthrough designation, and positive pivotal evidence; independent label/safety review unresolved.

predictions.level1ClinicalEvidence: Previously approved IV isatuximab with subcutaneous formulation and on-body administration, not a de novo myeloma efficacy molecule.
predictions.level2BenefitRisk: Patient convenience and established therapeutic activity favor bridging; infusion/injection tolerability, device reliability and pharmacokinetic comparability still required.
predictions.level3RegulatoryFit: Approval lean despite April major amendment and three-month extension; positive European CHMP opinion supports regulatory plausibility but is not FDA proof.

predictions.level1ClinicalEvidence: CARES-310 Phase 3 showed OS and PFS benefit against sorafenib; median OS sponsor-reported 23.8 months.
predictions.level2BenefitRisk: Clinically important first-line HCC efficacy and manageable reported safety; no guarantee of U.S. manufacturing acceptability.
predictions.level3RegulatoryFit: CRL lean: repeated prior FDA rejection cycles and unresolved facility/CMC inspection uncertainty make regulatory failure plausible despite strong efficacy; Feb resubmission and claimed fixes mitigate risk.

predictions.level1ClinicalEvidence: Phase 3 adult and pediatric ADHD efficacy previously reported; June 2026 3b comorbid anxiety study met primary symptom endpoint.
predictions.level2BenefitRisk: Meaningful ADHD symptom improvement with a triple monoamine reuptake mechanism; cardiovascular and psychiatric safety, controlled substance classification require attention.
predictions.level3RegulatoryFit: Approval lean after priority review acceptance and multiple positive Phase 3 trials, with label/scheduling uncertainty.

predictions.level1ClinicalEvidence: Supplemental device/drug application for a subcutaneous furosemide auto-injector; same furosemide platform already approved as an on-body infusor.
predictions.level2BenefitRisk: Clinical furosemide diuretic efficacy established, convenience and deliverability plausible; human factors, device precision and CMC matter.
predictions.level3RegulatoryFit: Approval lean for a delivery device supplement of marketed therapy, assuming device validation and manufacturing meet FDA standards.

predictions.level1ClinicalEvidence: Previously disputed NORSE clinical evidence; the FDA Office of New Drugs reversal in May found substantial evidence of effectiveness and no additional trials required.
predictions.level2BenefitRisk: Potential standardized ophthalmic bevacizumab formulation; past CRL and clinical trial inconsistency plus labeling/CMC remain risks.
predictions.level3RegulatoryFit: Approval lean based on Class 1 resubmission, appeal win on efficacy, and sponsor-reported move to final labeling, without assuming risk fully eliminated.

predictions.application: Gwyn Lo weekly low-estrogen contraceptive patch
predictions.level1ClinicalEvidence: Open-label Phase 3 contraceptive efficacy and adhesion study with favorable sponsor-reported findings; established transdermal contraceptive technology.
predictions.level2BenefitRisk: Contraceptive efficacy and adhesion support usability; thromboembolic risk, BMI restrictions and estrogen exposure require label safeguards.
predictions.level3RegulatoryFit: Approval lean on 505(b)(2) pathway, established Xulane platform, positive Phase 3 efficacy and FDA accepted application.
